extracted.intended_audience: general public / anyone converting heights or lengths between centimeters and feet/inches
extracted.subtask_short: cm to feet and inches conversion
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions, formulas, tables and worked examples for converting lengths (commonly heights) between centimeters and decimal feet and feet+inches, and for converting feet+inches back to centimeters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feet = Cm ÷ 30.48
rubrics_metrics.description: The formula for converting centimeters to feet is: Feet = Cm ÷ 30.48
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this formula to convert a cm value into decimal feet (e.g. 171 ÷ 30.48 = 5.61 ft).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feet and inches formula (use floor for whole feet)
rubrics_metrics.description: The formula for converting centimeters to feet AND inches is: Whole feet = floor(Cm ÷ 30.48) + Inches = (Cm ÷ 30.48 - Whole feet) × 12
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute whole feet by taking the floor of cm ÷ 30.48, then multiply the fractional remainder by 12 to get inches (fractional inches possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion methodology (step-by-step)
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert centimeters to feet, divide your cm figure by 30.48. To convert to feet and inches, divide your cm figure by 30.48 to get your feet and then multiply the remainder decimal by 12 to get your inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates the practical step sequence to follow for cm→ft and cm→ft+in conversions; follow with rounding as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion constants
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 12 inches in a foot. As there are 2.54 cm in an inch, there are 30.48 centimeters in one foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fixed factors (12, 2.54, 30.48) are the basis for all interconversions between cm, inches and feet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding conventions for tables and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: conversions are rounded to 2 decimal places. (In one table note: conversions are rounded to max 1 decimal place.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting results, apply the page's stated rounding rules: many charts round to two decimals; some chart entries use a maximum of one decimal. For human-facing height statements the page sometimes rounds to the nearest inch (e.g., '180cm is equal to 5 feet and 11 inches, rounded to the nearest inch').

rubrics_metrics.name: How to convert feet (or feet+inches) to cm
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert feet to centimeters, multiply your feet figure by 30.48 (cm = feet × 30.48). To convert from feet and inches, convert your feet figure to inches first (multiply it by 12), add on the inches remainder and then multiply the result by 2.54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (feet × 12 + inches) × 2.54 = centimeters. Use when converting human heights given in ft and in back to cm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worked example: cm to ft+in (Mabel, 171 cm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Mabel is 171cm tall. Height in feet = 171 ÷ 30.48 = 5.61 feet. Her height remainder in inches = 0.61 feet * 12 = 7.32 inches. Mabel's height is 5 feet 7.32 inches (5'7").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use worked examples to verify calculations and to illustrate fractional-inch results before rounding/presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worked example: ft+in to cm (James, 5 ft 10 in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: James is 5ft 10 inches tall. Height in inches only = (5 feet × 12) + 10 = 70 inches. Height in cm = 70 inches × 2.54 = 177.8cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the stepwise conversion from ft+in to cm and the final rounded cm value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table presentation: show both decimal feet and feet+inches
rubrics_metrics.description: Charts present columns for Centimeters | Feet (decimal) | Feet and inches (e.g. '165 cm | 5.41 ft | 5 ft. 5 in').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide convenient lookup tables for common values, showing both decimal-feet and feet+inches representations, and indicate the rounding policy used for the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct computation for specific ft+in to cm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this direct formula for converting a specific feet+inches measure into centimeters without first converting to decimal feet.
